# Zane Landers (AstroZane)

> Zane Landers is an amateur astronomer, telescope maker and science writer in Tucson, Arizona. He hosts private star parties in Tucson, Phoenix and across the Southwest through AstroZane, is Lead Writer and Editor of the telescope review site TelescopicWatch, writes for Live Science, serves on the founding board of DarkSky Southern Arizona and moderates r/telescopes.

## Star parties

- [Book a star party](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/): private, screen-free star parties for groups of 2 to 20, and larger events for up to 100 guests, with hand-built telescopes and night vision. Bookings open January through May 2027 and August through December 2027; June and July by request only.
- [Star party pricing](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/pricing/): every base price on one page. Per group, not per person. Tucson from $300 (1 hour), $400 (2 hours), $500 (3 hours), $550 (4 hours). Phoenix and Scottsdale from $500 (2 hours), $600 (3 hours), $700 (4 hours). Groups of 20 to 100 from $500 to $1,100. Destination trips from $600. Venues from $400.
- [Tucson and Southern Arizona](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/tucson/): base price from $300 per group for one hour.
- [Phoenix and Scottsdale](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/phoenix/): base price from $500 per group, two-hour minimum, travel included.
- Destination star parties (Sedona, Flagstaff, Grand Canyon, Organ Pipe Cactus, Cosmic Campground, City of Rocks and elsewhere in the Southwest): base price from $600, quoted individually.
- Larger events, Tucson area: from $500 for 20 to 40 guests, $700 for 40 to 70 and $999 for 70 to 100, with extra telescopes above 40.
- [Star parties for venues](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/venues/): resorts, hotels, guest ranches, vineyards, weddings and corporate events. Flat rate from $400 for two hours, recurring series from $250 a night, or ticketed with no cost up front. Venue dates open January through May 2027 and August through December 2027.
- Venues worked with: Mount Lemmon Lodge, White Stallion Ranch, Tucson Mountain Guest Ranch, and El Conquistador Tucson, A Hilton Resort.
- [Bachelor and bachelorette star parties in Scottsdale](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/starparties/scottsdale-bachelor-bachelorette/): at a rental or a dark-sky site about an hour from the Valley, base price from $500 for two hours.
- [Best stargazing spots near Tucson](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/stargazing-near-tucson/): more than 20 sites with drive times, including Sabino Canyon, Saguaro National Park, Gabe Zimmerman Trailhead, Ironwood Forest, three spots on Mount Lemmon (Windy Point Vista, Summerhaven and the summit), Empire Ranch, Tubac, the Whipple Observatory astronomy pads, Kartchner Caverns State Park, Apache Springs Trailhead, Oracle State Park, Buenos Aires National Wildlife Refuge, Patagonia Lake, Aravaipa Canyon west trailhead, Cochise Stronghold, Parker Canyon Lake, Montezuma Pass, Chiricahua National Park (Echo Canyon trailhead or Massai Point), Onion Saddle, Rustler Park and Mount Graham. Trailheads and other public land need no call ahead; national and state parks do.
- [Best stargazing spots near Phoenix and Scottsdale](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/stargazing-near-phoenix/): Fountain Hills, Badger Springs Trailhead, Picketpost Trailhead, Tonto National Forest, Hovatter Road, Roosevelt Lake and Alamo Lake.
- [Night vision astronomy explained](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/night-vision/): how a PVS-14 image intensifier shows nebulae live at the eyepiece, and how it differs from a smart telescope.
- [Sidewalk astronomy and public outreach](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/sidewalk-astronomy/): free looks at the Moon and planets on University Boulevard in Tucson and at public events, since 2022. Past outreach with the Westport Astronomical Society and Reach for the Stars Arizona; ongoing outreach with the Huachuca Astronomy Club.
- [Telescope repair and setup help](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/telescope-repair/): in-person collimation, troubleshooting and repair in Tucson and Phoenix.
- [Contact](https://astrozane.com/links/contact/): booking requests, telescope repair, and writing or marketing work.

## Telescopes and astrophotography

- [Current telescopes](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/telescopes/)
- [14.7-inch f/2.9 Dobsonian](https://astrozane.com/projects/147-inch-f29/): hand-built main telescope with a quartz mirror by Steve Dodds of Nova Optical.
- [24-inch f/4 Dobsonian](https://astrozane.com/projects/24-inch-f4/): a 2009 Eric Allen telescope being rebuilt, to be completed in 2027.
- 30-inch f/4.4 Starsplitter Dobsonian: built for Gary Myers, with a prototype ServoCAT; shared with Cole Rees and kept at Chiricahua Sky Village. Not available for star parties.
- Also in use: a 1980 Celestron C8, an SVBONY MK127 and a ZWO SeeStar S50 Pro.
- [Telescope restorations](https://astrozane.com/projects/restoration-projects/): a 1931 J.W. Fecker 3.5-inch refractor, a 1972 Celestron C8 and a 1959 Criterion RV-6, with before and after photos.
- Earlier builds: a 20.5-inch f/4.5 Dobsonian with a spray-silvered mirror, a 16-inch f/4.9 Dobsonian, a 10-inch f/3.2 Newtonian, and design work on the 3D-printed Hadley 114.
- Smart telescopes: has owned and reviewed nearly every smart telescope on the market for TelescopicWatch, including ZWO Seestar, Dwarf and Vaonis Vespera models.
- [Telescope FOV and magnification calculator](https://astrozane.com/calculators/FOV/)
- [Telescope limiting magnitude calculator](https://astrozane.com/calculators/limiting-magnitude/): faintest star or deep-sky surface brightness for a given telescope, sky and observer.
- [Astrophotography](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/astrophotography/)

## About, press and speaking

- [About Zane Landers: press and speaking](https://astrozane.com/about/press/): coverage in TIME, National Geographic, The Guardian and Sky & Telescope, recorded talks, and booking for talks on telescope making, night vision astronomy, public outreach and smart telescopes.

## Elsewhere

- [TelescopicWatch](https://telescopicwatch.com/): hands-on telescope rankings, reviews and buying guides edited by Zane Landers.
- [Protecting dark skies in Tucson and Southern Arizona](https://astrozane.com/astronomy/dark-skies/): what light pollution is, how it affects health and wildlife, what dark skies are worth to the local economy, where Tucson's light comes from (streetlights are only about 14 percent of the skyglow), why prisons are a major source and how they can be lit with shielded fixtures, a concept map of a proposed Copper Corridor dark sky area covering the San Pedro, Aravaipa and upper Gila valleys, the Superstitions and Tonto Basin, what DarkSky International and DarkSky Southern Arizona each do, and how to help.
- [DarkSky Southern Arizona](https://darkskysoaz.org/): regional chapter of DarkSky International; donations at https://darkskysoaz.org/donate/.
- [Observational Astronomy Discord](https://discord.gg/astronomy): community for telescope help and observing.
- [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/astrozane): professional background; open to full-time marketing, communications and content roles.
